# 2.1.0: what was measured, in full

The 2.1.0 release notes in `2.1.0.md` state the shape of the change and the two headline figures.
This file holds the detail behind them: the report movement project by project, the folders the
new slice resolver merges, and the folder spellings the punctuation case was checked against.

## How this was measured

Eight public FSD projects, pinned to fixed commits, linted twice from the same checkouts at
default options and with the same configuration: once with the plugin built at the 2.1.0 branch
point, which is 2.0.1 behaviour, and once with the release. The eight are
`buggregator-frontend`, `cloudhood`, `moonlogs`, `nukeapp`, `polka`, `vkui-audiopad`,
`workout-cool` and `yeahub-platform`. The merged groups below were resolved file by file with the
release's own resolver over the same eight checkouts.

Both directions are given separately throughout, because a net figure hides a swap.

## Report movement

Together the eight hold 4071 linted files. 2.0.1 produced 6600 reports on them and this release
produces 6597. Thirteen reports appeared and sixteen disappeared. Nothing crashed on either
version.

| project | linted files | reports on 2.0.1 | reports here | new | gone |
| - | -: | -: | -: | -: | -: |
| `buggregator-frontend` | 523 | 19 | 20 | 1 | 0 |
| `cloudhood` | 204 | 404 | 402 | 0 | 2 |
| `moonlogs` | 248 | 411 | 409 | 0 | 2 |
| `nukeapp` | 162 | 52 | 52 | 0 | 0 |
| `polka` | 60 | 11 | 11 | 0 | 0 |
| `vkui-audiopad` | 181 | 9 | 5 | 0 | 4 |
| `workout-cool` | 416 | 1409 | 1415 | 12 | 6 |
| `yeahub-platform` | 2277 | 4285 | 4283 | 0 | 2 |
| total | 4071 | 6600 | 6597 | 13 | 16 |

Per rule and message id, for every project on which anything moved:

| project | rule | message id | new | gone |
| - | - | - | -: | -: |
| `buggregator-frontend` | `public-api` | `should-be-from-public-api` | 1 | 0 |
| `cloudhood` | `layers-slices` | `can-not-import` | 0 | 2 |
| `moonlogs` | `public-api` | `should-be-from-public-api` | 0 | 2 |
| `vkui-audiopad` | `layers-slices` | `can-not-import` | 0 | 4 |
| `workout-cool` | `absolute-relative` | `must-be-relative-path` | 10 | 0 |
| `workout-cool` | `layers-slices` | `can-not-import` | 1 | 6 |
| `workout-cool` | `public-api` | `should-be-from-public-api` | 1 | 0 |
| `yeahub-platform` | `layers-slices` | `can-not-import` | 0 | 1 |
| `yeahub-platform` | `public-api` | `should-be-from-public-api` | 0 | 1 |

Nothing moved at all on `nukeapp` or on `polka`.

Across all eight, by rule and message id:

| rule | message id | new | gone |
| - | - | -: | -: |
| `absolute-relative` | `must-be-relative-path` | 10 | 0 |
| `layers-slices` | `can-not-import` | 1 | 13 |
| `public-api` | `should-be-from-public-api` | 2 | 3 |

`import-order` did not move on any of the eight, in either direction, and `layers-slices`
`pass-through-reexport`, the message id this release adds, did not fire once on any of them at
default options.

Of the thirteen that appeared, exactly one came from a re-export becoming visible, on
`workout-cool`'s `src/features/workout-builder/index.ts`, which forwards a sibling slice on its
third line; the other twelve follow from the slice boundary moving. Ten of those twelve are
`absolute-relative` `must-be-relative-path` and two are `public-api`
`should-be-from-public-api`. Of the sixteen that disappeared, fourteen come from
the merged folders enumerated below and two from the segment prefix fix: both of those are in
`moonlogs`, where 2.0.1 named `@/features-token/api-token-create` and
`@/features-token/api-token-edit` for imports of `@/features/api-token/api-token-create` and
`@/features/api-token/api-token-edit`.

These are eight specific codebases, not a forecast for yours. What the tables do show is the shape
to expect: the movement is concentrated in the three rules that depend on where a slice begins, it
lands on a handful of projects rather than spreading evenly, and both directions occur in the same
release.

## The folders that merge into their slice

A merged group is a folder the resolver settles on for two or more of the slice names the old path
heuristic derived. Every name in the group except one is a folder inside the slice rather than a
slice of its own, so an import between two of them stops being a cross slice import and its report
disappears.

Exactly one member of every group below carries a public api file of its own. That member is
marked `[barrel]` and is the folder the group collapses onto. The failure this design exists to
avoid, two or more merged names each carrying a public api file, occurs in none of the 23 on any
of the eight projects: it would silence a genuine cross slice report, and it would be a reason to
stop the release rather than a line in this file.

### Calibration: 5 of the 23 move a report, 18 move none

A merged group is not the same thing as a lost report. A group only costs a report when something
actually imports across two of the merged names, and most of them have nothing crossing. Of the 23
groups, **5 move a report and the other 18 move none**: `sortable-list` in `cloudhood`,
`album-list` and `track-list` in `vkui-audiopad`, `workout-builder` in `workout-cool` and
`SubscriptionsList` in `yeahub-platform`, which between them account for the 14 disappearing
reports that this class contributes.

Thirteen of the fourteen are the same picture: a slice folder holding an `index.ts`, sub-folders
beside it holding none, and a file in one sub-folder importing another. The sub-folder holding the
importing file was one of `__tests__`, `actions`, `hooks`, `libs/hooks`, `gallery` and `list`; on
the imported side the folders were `actions`, `album`, `hooks`, `libs/constants`, `schema` and
`track`. The fourteenth differs only in its target, which lies directly in the slice folder rather
than in a second sub-folder.

### Total

**23 merged groups across the eight projects.** The names in each row are the last path part of the
folder the old heuristic would have called a slice, which is why two rows can both name `gallery`
or `hooks`.

## The folder spellings behind the punctuation case

The release notes state that a folder name carrying punctuation no longer hides its slice. These
are the spellings that was measured on, with an `index.ts` on the slice folder in each case.

In group position, above the slice: `(shop)`, `[shop]`, `shop.group` and `shop+group`, all of
which hid the slice on 2.0.1 and no longer do. At slice position, directly on the layer: `(user)`
and `user+x`, the same way.

The controls are the plainly spelled names in the same positions, `shop-group`, `_shop` and
`user`, which reported on both versions and from every importer tried. So the effect turns on the
spelling and not on grouping.

The importing side has to resolve as well, because if either side of a comparison is unresolved
both fall back to the old path heuristic together. With the slice at `entities/(shop)/ShopA`, an
importer at `src/pages/home/index.ts` reports, and so does one at `src/pages/home/ui/Page.ts` when
`pages/home` holds an `index.ts` of its own. The same importer at `src/pages/home/ui/Page.ts` with
no `index.ts` on `pages/home`, and one at `src/pages/home/A.ts` in a `home` folder holding no
`index` file at all, are both silent.
